newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sees lower budget surplus this year.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sees lower budget surplus this year.

text.p: The Philippine government may likely post a lower budget surplus of 7.1 billion pesos this year, almost half of the 13 billion-peso surplus it targetted for the year, according to documents from the Development Budget Coordination Committee released on Thursday.

The smaller surplus would be the result of lower revenues due to the possibility of high tax exemptions based on a bill passed by the House of Representatives, lower privatisation proceeds and other factors.
As of the first five months of this year, the budget surplus was estimated at 4.9 billion pesos, the documents showed. In the first four months, the surplus was 18.2 billion pesos.
Budget officials said the government would also have to cut its expenditures to achieve a surplus this year.
"It is, therefore, imperative that the national government maintain a reasonable surplus position to put across a strong signal to the market of a healthy fiscal position," the papers said.
It cited the positive effects of the surplus on prices and foreign exchange rates.
